note_sections.t: Re-evaluation for definitive management of high-volume, high-grade prostate adenocarcinoma following a dramatic PSA surge to 190.0 ng/mL.

This 57-year-old retired accountant presents for re-evaluation of his known prostate cancer. His PSA trajectory has been steep, rising from 3.0 ng/mL in mid-2022 to 16.4 ng/mL in April 2024, and now 190.0 ng/mL this February. He lives alone, though his unmarried partner serves as his primary next-of-kin and support. He reports moderate lower urinary tract symptoms, quantified by an IPSS of 15. He is a non-smoker, consumes approximately 8 units of alcohol weekly, and maintains an active lifestyle with cycling five times a week for commuting. He has a background of chronic kidney disease, with recent labs showing an eGFR below 60 mL/min/1.73m2. He recently attended a dermatology appointment for a routine check of actinic keratoses. He prefers morning appointments due to reliance on public transport.

On DRE, the prostate is smooth, symmetric, and non-tender, with no palpable nodules or asymmetry, consistent with clinical stage cT1c. The patient is in no acute distress, and general examination is unremarkable with stable vital signs.
